$comment: How old a reading is, in the words every Quota client uses. One rule, one voice: the menu bar footer, a provider row, a device row, the website, and the widgets all state age relative to now rather than as a clock time or a calendar date, because an absolute instant makes the reader do the subtraction. `age` is the bare relative phrase; `observation` is the whole line under a reading, which names why a reading is not current instead of only that it is not; `device` is the age half of a device row. `packages/apple-shared` and `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts` both answer this file, so a phrase one of them changes cannot drift from the other.

age.name: under a minute reads as an instant, not a ticking second count
the last second before a minute is still an instant
a whole minute is the first age worth a number
minutes run to the last one before an hour
hours run to the last one before a day
days run to the last one before a week
weeks run to the last one before a year
a reading stamped in the future is not negative

observation.name: a current reading says when it was taken
a current reading hours old still says so plainly
a reading that aged out says it is not current
a source that lost its sign-in names that instead
a source that could not be reached names that instead
a source that cannot answer at all names that instead
a source that failed names that instead

device.name: a device that reported a week ago
a device the Account has never heard from
